blocks.text: 1. Traditional Search vs RAG

blocks.alt: Keyword search is compared against RAG, which combines semantic search and generation

blocks.text: Traditional Search vs RAG closes out this module with a grounding comparison between classic search and modern retrieval.
It compares keyword search, already familiar to most people, against modern retrieval and generation.
2. Recapping The Preview
Types of RAG's closing recap previewed this comparison as closing the module with a classic search comparison, briefly described there.
This topic gives that preview its complete, dedicated treatment, exploring every detail only briefly hinted at before.
3. Recapping Retrieval Using Embeddings
What Is RAG introduced RAG's own retrieval step: it searches by semantic meaning, not exact words.
Traditional search works on an entirely different underlying principle instead.
4. Keyword Matching Explained

blocks.alt: Query terms go through exact text matching to produce results

blocks.text: Traditional search matches exact or near-exact words between a query and a document.
A document containing none of the query's literal words never gets returned at all.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Search style","What it matches on"],"rows":[["Traditional keyword search","Exact or near-exact words"],["Semantic search","Meaning, regardless of exact wording"]]}

blocks.text: 5. Semantic Search Explained

blocks.alt: Query meaning goes through embedding similarity to produce results

blocks.text: RAG's own retrieval instead compares meaning, using cosine similarity as covered in Sentence Embeddings.
A document can match a query even when no exact words overlap at all.
6. The Synonym And Paraphrase Problem

blocks.alt: The keyword car misses the paraphrase automobile

blocks.text: Searching for automobile, keyword search misses a document that only says car.
Semantic search catches that paraphrased match instead, a concrete, real-world example of the difference.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This paraphrase advantage explains why RAG systems tend to feel more forgiving of natural, conversational queries than classic keyword search engines ever were.

blocks.text: 7. When Traditional Search Still Wins

blocks.alt: Exact code or ID search favors keyword search

blocks.text: Exact identifiers, like product codes or error messages, favor keyword matching instead.
Semantic similarity can sometimes blur exactly the precision that matters there, an honest, balanced limitation.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Query type","Better suited approach"],"rows":[["Exact codes or error messages","Traditional keyword search"],["Natural, conversational questions","Semantic search"]]}

blocks.text: 8. Preview Of Hybrid Search

blocks.alt: Keyword search combines with semantic search

blocks.text: Combining both approaches captures the strengths of each at once.
Hybrid Search, covered as its own dedicated topic later in this course, explores that combined approach.
9. Generation Is The New Part

blocks.alt: Traditional search returns documents while RAG generates an answer

blocks.text: Traditional search returns a ranked list of documents for a person to read.
RAG adds the generation stage, covered generally in What Is RAG, producing one direct answer instead. That is the final, key distinction between the two.
10. Recognizing When RAG Is Preferable To Traditional Search Alone
RAG handles paraphrased queries and produces direct answers.
Traditional keyword search remains better for exact identifiers and codes.

blocks.text: 12. Common Mistakes

items: Assuming semantic search always outperforms keyword search in every situation.
Using pure semantic search for exact identifiers like product codes, where precision matters most.
Forgetting that traditional search returns a list for a person to read, while RAG generates a direct answer.
Overlooking hybrid search when a real system needs both precision and paraphrase tolerance.

blocks.text: 13. RAG Fundamentals: Module Complete

items: Traditional search matches exact or near-exact words; RAG's retrieval matches semantic meaning.
A document with none of the query's literal words never gets returned by keyword search.
Semantic search can match a document even when no exact words overlap at all.
Keyword search misses paraphrases like automobile versus car; semantic search catches them.
Exact identifiers and codes still favor traditional keyword matching over semantic similarity.
Hybrid search combines both approaches to capture the strengths of each.
Traditional search returns a ranked list to read; RAG generates one direct answer instead.
RAG suits paraphrased, conversational queries; traditional search suits exact identifiers.
